tpm_manager: rewrite context connection logic for TPM1.2 The current implementation is not accurate and has many defects: 1. error handling for communication failure doesn't consider the error layer. 2. 1 excessive 100ms sleep upon consistent communication failure. 3. when consistent communication failure, the logic falls the nullified checking, which gives a confusing message "Enexpected NULL context.", while it should be logging communication failure. 4. over-complicated loop for the retry loigc and unnecessarily deep nested loop. 5. context doesn't get reset after failed communication, which means the user could get an disconnected context for the second call of |GetContext|. BUG=b:138288163 BUG=b:137707011 TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-chell tpm_manager TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-soraka tpm_manager TEST=tpm_manager_client read_space --index=0x10000001 --file=/dev/null Change-Id: Ib41ba71e9baf01dc368b4798ba2a3c15bafcc4f9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1716774 Tested-by: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com> Commit-Ready: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: bluetooth: xbox controller bug fix The current L2CAP implementation does not change any options if the other side respons with "unknown options", but does if "unaccepted options" is the answer. It is up to the implementation to decide on the effort spent on config negotiations, therefore the current implementation is correct at this point - but many devices (like Xbox One S controllers) are not useable this way. A workaround for many users therefore is to disable_ertm, since this is often the option which is unknown. I would prefer to try it again with altered options instead of globally disable ERTM. In result, I suggest the following patch. It simply adds a new case (L2CAP_CONF_UNKNOWN), which does nothing but falling through to L2CAP_CONF_UNACCEPT. iproute2: Resync ARL qdisc attributes The ARL qdisc defines several Netlink attributes that are 64bit quantities. With the introduction of the nla_put_u64_64bit() helper [commit 73520786b079 ("libnl: add nla_put_u64_64bit() helper")] these attributes are forced to 64bit alignment. A new ARL attribute (TCA_ARL_PAD) is defined in the kernel pkt_sched.h file, which is inserted in the Netlink message when padding is required to achieve the necessary 64bit attribute alignment. The iproute2 package maintains its own private copy of the kernel pkt_sched.h file. This CL synchronizes the kernel TCA_ARL_xxx attribute list with the iproute2 private pkt_sched.h, this picks up the new TCA_ARL_PAD to ensure the 'tc qdisc show' command can properly recognize and decode Netlink messages when ARL Qdisc is active. BUG=b:138685581 TEST=System test: % tc qdisc add dev wan0 root handle 1: arl minrate 4800kbit \ buffer 5000 limit 500 latency 100ms latency_hysteresis 30ms % tc -s qdisc show dev wan0 Change-Id: I81aaedb904b4b8afffd879380faad72e60600ab3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1732488 Tested-by: Danny Mitzel <mitzel@google.com> Commit-Ready: Danny Mitzel <mitzel@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: bluetooth: xbox controller bug fix The current L2CAP implementation does not change any options if the other side respons with "unknown options", but does if "unaccepted options" is the answer. It is up to the implementation to decide on the effort spent on config negotiations, therefore the current implementation is correct at this point - but many devices (like Xbox One S controllers) are not useable this way. A workaround for many users therefore is to disable_ertm, since this is often the option which is unknown. I would prefer to try it again with altered options instead of globally disable ERTM. In result, I suggest the following patch. It simply adds a new case (L2CAP_CONF_UNKNOWN), which does nothing but falling through to L2CAP_CONF_UNACCEPT.
